easy.p1: In Konta an invoice looks like an invoice. You can see straight away what needs filling in, and whatever is calculated for you stays out of the way.
easy.p2: The interface is in Romanian and Russian. Account names in the chart of accounts are in Romanian for now, as the Ministry of Finance order gives them, and Russian names will follow. The terms come from the national accounting standards and the Tax Code, the way you say them every day.
easy.p3: When something goes wrong, a person answers the phone, in Romanian or Russian.

ef.caveat: Every rule here is in our public register, with a reference to the legal act. A licensed accountant is still checking the values.
ef.law.p1: Today e-Factura is mandatory in four cases: supplies to state institutions and in public procurement, supplies to agents with no fiscal relationship with the budget (since 1 January 2025), supplies for the projects named in art. 104(c¹) of the Tax Code, and companies that SFS has put on its risk list.
ef.law.p2: International VAT trackers wrote that e-Factura would become mandatory for every company on 1 October 2026. That date has passed, and as of 15 October 2026 no Moldovan legal act sets it: for every other VAT payer, e-Factura remains optional. The list of companies that must use it grows through SFS orders; the latest, Order 494 of 2 October 2026, added six companies. If an obligation for everyone is adopted, we’ll add it to the register and say so here.
ef.law.p3: From 1 January 2026 the rule that denied a buyer the VAT deduction on a paper invoice from a listed supplier was repealed.
ef.law.p4: A VAT refund is capped at a share of the VAT that buyers paid, documented through e-Factura and through cash registers connected to MEV. Government Decision 496/2025 raised that share from 20% to 70% from 14 August 2025.
ef.law.title: What the law says today

ef.p1: Konta will bring the electronic invoices of all your client companies onto one screen. Purchase invoices that arrive as XML will become drafts in the books, which the accountant checks and posts. The sales and purchase registers will be filled from what has already gone through SFS, so nothing will have to be typed in twice.
ef.title: e-Factura for all your clients, on one screen
ef.today.p1: Konta’s e-Factura client already talks to SFS’s e-Factura test service: it sends drafts, finds them again, and looks up taxpayers and their registered bank accounts. Signing, and bringing received invoices into the books, come next. The client’s code is public, for anyone to read.

move.p1: Send us the trial balance from 1C as at your switch-over date, and we open the company in Konta with the same balances. We move each accounting firm’s first company ourselves, free of charge. You’ll be able to move the rest yourself, from the same kind of file.
move.p2: The side-by-side period lasts as long as you need. Konta takes over the account balances at the switch-over date, and the documents from before it stay in 1C. The switch rests on reconciled numbers you can check yourself.
move.s1: You export the trial balance from 1C as at the date you choose (xlsx or csv).
move.s2: We open the company in Konta with the same balances.
move.s3: You work in both programs side by side and compare the totals.
move.s4: You leave 1C only once the numbers match.

np.meta.title: Accounting without a programmer · Konta
np.p1: In a program where tax rules live in the code, every new law means paying a programmer to come and rewrite it, separately on each installation. Konta keeps the law as data. We change it once and every customer has it the same day.
np.p2: The bill on the 2027 fiscal and customs policy (no. 326) passed its first reading on 10 September 2026 and may change before the second. This is what it changes, as it stands:
np.p3: In an ordinary program, each row of this table is another call to the programmer. In Konta we enter them in the public register ourselves, citing the bill, where anyone can check them. Once the law is adopted, we update the values once, for every client. You don’t pay extra for that.

priv.basis.p1: We answer because you wrote to us: answering a message we receive is our legitimate interest, and you are expecting that answer. When you ask for a demo or an offer, the processing is a step we take at your request before a possible contract. Limiting messages by IP address protects the form from abuse, also in our legitimate interest. You can object at any time to processing based on our legitimate interest.
priv.basis.p2: The bases are those in art. 6(1)(b) and (f) of Law No. 195/2024 on personal data protection, in force since 23 August 2026.
priv.changes.p: If we change how we use data, we update this page and the date above. A change that would need new consent does not apply without it.
priv.cookies.p1: The site uses no analytics, tracking or advertising tools and loads nothing from other sites. In your browser it keeps only the language and theme you choose: the konta_lang and konta_theme cookies, with konta_lang_at and konta_theme_at recording when you chose. They are shared with app.konta.md, so the app opens in the same language and theme, and they last a year. The same two values are also kept in the browser's storage (konta.lang, konta.theme).
priv.keep.p1: Messages and enquiries that do not lead to working together: at most 12 months after the last exchange, then we delete them. If the conversation becomes a contract, the contract documents are kept as long as the law requires.
priv.keep.p2: The counter that limits messages keeps your IP address for at most an hour after your last attempt, then deletes it.
priv.meta.description: What the contact form on konta.md sends us, why, how long we keep it, and how to ask us to show, correct or delete it.
priv.meta.title: Privacy · Konta
priv.p1: In short: we use what you send through the contact form to answer you and, if you ask for a demo, to contact you about Konta. We do not sell it or pass it to anyone for marketing, and the site does not track you.
priv.rights.p1: Under Law No. 195/2024 (art. 15-21) you can ask what data we hold about you and get a copy, ask us to correct or delete it or to restrict its processing, have it given to you in a format you can use elsewhere, and object to processing based on our legitimate interest. Write to mail@konta.md: we answer within one working day.
priv.rights.p2: You also have the right to complain to the National Center for Personal Data Protection of the Republic of Moldova or to go to court.
priv.title: Privacy
priv.to.p1: Our hosting and email provider: the site, the form and the mailbox your message arrives in are with them.
priv.to.p2: The Konta app’s database (app.konta.md): every message also arrives there, as an enquiry we follow until it is answered. The app’s server is currently rented from the same hosting provider.
priv.to.p3: No one else. We do not sell, rent or pass on data for marketing.
priv.what.p1: The contact form: your name, email address and message (required), your company and phone number (optional), the topic you pick from the list, and the language you were reading the page in. We use them to answer you and, if you ask for a demo, to contact you about Konta. Without a name, an email address and a message we cannot answer you; the rest you give only if you want to. We take no automated decisions based on this data.
priv.what.p2: The IP address the form is sent from. The server uses it to limit how many messages can be sent, at most five an hour from one address, so the form cannot be used for spam. We also pass it to the Konta app with your message, for the same limit.
priv.what.p3: If you email or call us directly, we receive only what you tell or send us there.
priv.who.p: The data controller is December Capital SRL, IDNO 1005600041997, str. M. Sadoveanu 28, Chișinău MD-2075, Republic of Moldova. We make Konta and run konta.md. For any question about your data, write to mail@konta.md.
